segments.en: Otzar HaYirah — Treasury of Awe | Volume IV (נ–ת)

This brief but profound chapter reveals the kabbalistic mechanics of the redemption-gift (pidyon). Money is not merely a financial transaction — in Breslov teaching it is an aspect of divine judgment (dinim), rooted in the left side (smol) and in the world of number and count, which is by nature deficient. When money is brought to the true Tzadik, it ascends to the root of sustenance — the level of mazal, above number and judgment — and through this all judgments are sweetened at their source.

Entry 5 is the most expansive, tracing the entire chain: the flaw of da'as (diverting the mind from constant G-d-awareness) → damage to the illumination of the Will (ha'aras haratzon) → flaw of eating → all suffering. The rectification runs in reverse: giving a pidyon to the Tzadik → his eating becomes a vehicle for the illumination of the Will → all deficiencies are filled. This teaching echoes the sin of the primordial Adam, whose eating corrupted the world — and shows that rectification, too, passes through the channel of eating when that eating is connected to the Tzadik's holy da'as.

Entry 2 contains a poignant warning: even the Tzadik's prayers ascend for everyone — but disputing him actively delays redemption, as the Prophet cried: "I would have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against Me."
